alternatives.argument: The finished local proof establishes the theorem from the exact same-metric packing, sieve-tail and KL/log-square prior-mass premises: the denominator lemma gives the in-probability lower bound, the shell lemma supplies tests, and a direct tested-numerator/sieve-tail split yields the conclusion. The independent full-text alternative is Kleijn, Bayesian Statistics for Frequentists, Theorem 6.4.3 and its proof, supported by Ghosal 2010 §2.5.2. The source itself is not substituted for the local proof.

The finished local proof constructs the Hellinger product-affinity test, the full-L1 sign test and the uniformly bounded-L2 linear test, then uses finite block amplification and a shellwise union bound. Kleijn 2025 §6.4.4 and Ghosal 2010 §2.5.2 independently support the Hellinger covering/test route; Tropp Lecture 4 supports the bounded-sum Bernstein step. The L1/L2 extensions are proved locally.

The finished local proof establishes measurability, finite positive evidence, and the denominator bound by averaging the log likelihood over the local prior set, using Jensen, the finite-sum variance identity and Chebyshev. Kleijn 2025 Lemma 6.4.5 and Ghosal 2010 §2.5.2 give independent full-text treatments of this Jensen/Chebyshev lower bound.

The finished example verifies the global packing bound, zero sieve tail, local KL/log-square mass and theorem application for a compact Bernoulli parameter interval. Ghosal 2010 §2.5.3 independently records the finite-dimensional logarithmic overhead under the basic global-entropy theorem.

The local definition fixes the root-L2 normalization for two supplied unit-mass densities and proves finiteness by (sqrt(p)-sqrt(q))^2<=p+q; the GGV copy is unnecessary to the argument, and the full-text Ghosal 2010 and Kleijn 2025 treatments provide independent convention context.

The local proof uses L2 Minkowski and Cauchy-Schwarz, derives event-supremum TV as half the density L1 distance by threshold sets without sigma-finiteness, and proves the two Hellinger inequalities pointwise. Ghosal 2010 §2.5.2 and Kleijn 2025 §6.4 provide independent full-text comparison context.

The example proves only the conditional rate balance from its explicit same-metric packing and local-mass assumptions; Ghosal 2010 §2.5.3 is the retrieved full-text alternative rate discussion. It does not assert a generic entropy or prior-mass theorem.

This is an original local Bernoulli point-prior construction: a separated grid violates the chosen entropy inequality, while exact likelihood normalization leaves the posterior at the truth for every data vector. The theorem conditions are supported by the retrieved Kleijn 2025 and Ghosal 2010 full texts; no counterexample is attributed to the inaccessible GGV copy.
